# NGS Workflow: Automated, Scalable, Reproducible, and Portable Sequence Quality Control & Alignment Workflow

author: Stefanie Moreno
date: October 5, 2026

## Overview:

NGS Workflow is a reproducible, stage-driven next-generation sequencing (NGS) pipeline 
designed for automated retrieval, preprocessing, quality control assessment, contamination 
removal, alignment, indexing, statistics calculation, and reporting of paired-end runs.

The project combines:

* Bash for orchestration and resource management
* Python for configuration validation and stage resolution
* Snakemake for standardized workflow management and dependency tracking
* Conda for environment management
* Industry-standard bioinformatics tools for integrated QC metrics and alignment statistics
* Rigorous Python testing suite covering configuration validation, stage resolution, 
  resource requirements, error handling, and shell-safe variable generation
* Extensive dependencies file allowing for further workflow expansion
* Consolidation of actionable insights into a single dashboard deliverable
* Full parameterization allowing use with additional sequencing runs/reference genomes/adapters
* Multicore thread specification for non-limited tools
* Cross-platform compatibility 
* Strict Git version control
* Comprehensive logging and benchmarks written to separate dedicated files
* Configuration-driven resource retrieval with automated retry and recovery logic
* Full workflow execution or stage specification

The pipeline automatically:

* Retrieves paired-end sequencing reads from ENA or user-specified URLs
* Verifies download integrity through MD5 checksums
* Performs baseline and post-processing quality control assessments for comparison
* Removes specified adapters and contaminant sequences
* Aligns cleaned reads to a reference genome
* Removes PCR duplicates
* Indexes the deduplicated alignment BAM for downstream access and analysis
* Generates overview and comprehensive alignment statistics
* Produces a stage-specific or full-workflow MultiQC dashboard deliverable
* Reports status updates throughout execution to the terminal
* Tracks workflow runtime sans file retrieval/checks, reference indexing, and dry run
* Avoids file retrieval if already present within project, saving time and memory space


## Objective:

The primary goal of this project was to create a robust, portable, and innovative program 
that provides a comprehensive analysis of an NGS paired-end run, including baseline and 
post-processing quality control assessments to evaluate the benefits of trimming, 
decontamination, and deduplication. The quality control assessment stage of the program
is also accompanied by the alignment stage, in which the processed reads are aligned to
the reference genome, pcr duplicates are removed, and the resulting alignment is indexed.
EAch stage can be run individually or the entire workflow can be run at once, with all
executions requiring a single command. All workflow executions output a multiqc dashboard 
deliverable that consolidates the results from all steps in the specified execution into 
a unified and detailed visual summarization.

The workflow was designed around automation, modularity, validation, reproducibility, 
and future extensibility. For example:

**Automation**

This program is engineered to reduce manual downloading and handling of sequencing datasets,
as well as the reference genome and processing resources. The forward and reverse read 
files, reference genome, and the adapters to be trimmed during processing are all 
parameterized such that the user defines them by accession identifier and website urls in
the configuration file. The bash script performs checks to ensure each file is not already 
present inside the project directory before committing to retrieval, avoiding a waste of 
time and space, which becomes particularly useful as the genome size increases.

The bash script also auto-executes the indexing of the reference genome and performs a
dry run to confirm the validity of the project file and folder structuring prior to
the implementation run so there are no unexpected crashes due to structure inconsistencies
or missing requirements. It automatically tracks the runtime upon initiating execution of
the workflow, then updates the user upon pipeline completion with the total runtime and
location of the deliverables associated with the chosen workflow stage(s).

**Modularity**

The workflow was built around a stage-driven execution model that separates orchestration,
validation, resource provisioning, and workflow execution into independent components.

The Bash launcher manages environment validation, resource retrieval, checksum verification
, and stage execution. Configuration validation and stage resolution are handled 
independently through the Python stage registry, while workflow execution is delegated 
entirely to Snakemake. This separation of concerns allows components to be tested, 
modified, and expanded independently without requiring extensive changes elsewhere in the 
project.

The pipeline also supports targeted execution through stage-specific workflow targets. 
Users may execute only the quality-control workflow, only the alignment workflow, or the 
complete workflow while preserving dependency tracking and reproducibility.

The architecture was specifically designed to support future analytical modules such as:

* Variant Calling
* Assembly
* Annotation
* Coverage Analysis
* AMR Detection
* Taxonomic Classification

without requiring extensive changes to the underlying execution framework.


**Validation**

Extensive validation is performed before workflow execution begins to prevent resource 
waste and unexpected runtime failures.

The Bash launcher validates:

* Correct Conda environment activation
* Configuration file existence
* Download success
* File integrity through MD5 checksum verification

The Python stage registry independently validates:

* Stage names
* Stage implementation status
* Required configuration parameters
* Resource requirements for selected stages
* YAML syntax and readability

Invalid workflow requests are intercepted before Snakemake execution begins, allowing 
clear user-facing error messages to be reported without generating confusing stack traces 
or partial workflow outputs.

To further improve reliability, the workflow performs a Snakemake dry run before execution,
ensuring that all dependencies, file paths, and workflow targets can be successfully 
resolved.

**Reproducibility**

Reproducibility was a primary design goal throughout development.

All workflow behavior is driven through a centralized configuration file, allowing new 
sequencing runs, reference genomes, adapters, contaminants, and computational resources 
to be defined without modifying workflow code. Workflow execution is managed through 
Snakemake, which tracks file dependencies, execution order, and file generation history.

The project environment is fully defined through a Conda environment specification file, 
ensuring tool versions and software dependencies remain consistent between users and 
computing environments.

Comprehensive runtime logging and benchmark generation provide additional transparency 
by documenting tool execution, resource utilization, and performance characteristics for 
every workflow step.

Together, configuration-driven execution, environment standardization, dependency 
management, logging, benchmarking, and version control ensure analyses can be reproduced 
consistently across systems and over time.

**Extensibility**

Future expansion was considered during initial project design rather than added as an 
afterthought.

The centralized stage registry provides a single location where execution stages, 
required parameters, resource requirements, and Snakemake targets are defined. New 
workflow modules can therefore be integrated by extending the stage registry and 
implementing corresponding Snakemake rules without redesigning existing infrastructure.

Workflow staging currently supports:

* QC
* Alignment
* Complete Workflow Execution

while placeholders already exist for:

* Variant Calling
* Assembly
* Annotation
* Coverage Analysis
* AMR Detection
* Taxonomic Classification

The dashboard architecture was likewise extended to support stage-specific deliverables. 
Quality-control workflows, alignment workflows, and complete workflow executions each 
generate dedicated reporting outputs, allowing future modules to contribute their own 
stage-specific dashboards while remaining compatible with consolidated end-to-end 
reporting.



Additional processing steps that will be included as expansions include:

* coordinate sorting 
* fixing mate information
* hard filtering

The gradual expansion of this program will also include the following downstream analyses:



Automation

Reduce manual handling of sequencing datasets and reference resources.

Reproducibility

Ensure identical analyses can be reproduced through configuration-driven execution.

Robustness

Handle:

download failures
corrupted files
invalid configurations
missing resources

before workflow execution begins.

Extensibility

Support future workflow expansion through a centralized stage registry architecture.

## Stage-Based Execution Model

Rather than exposing every Snakemake rule directly, the project exposes workflow stages.

**QC Stage**

```Shell
./scripts/run_pipeline.sh --stage qc
```

Performs:


Baseline FastQC
↓
Adapter Trimming
↓
Decontamination
↓
Post-QC FastQC


Reference genome not required.

**Alignment Stage**

```Shell
./scripts/run_pipeline.sh --stage align
```

Performs:

QC Workflow
↓
BWA Alignment
↓
Duplicate Removal
↓
BAM Indexing
↓
Flagstat
↓
Alignment Statistics

Reference genome required.


**Full Pipeline**

```Shell
./scripts/run_pipeline.sh
````

or

```Shell
./scripts/run_pipeline.sh --stage all
```

Performs:

QC Workflow
↓
Alignment Workflow
↓
MultiQC Dashboard

## Tool Documentation

1. FastQC:

*Background*

FastQC is a sequencing quality assessment tool developed specifically for high-throughput 
sequencing datasets.

Purpose

Evaluate:

per-base quality
GC content
duplication levels
overrepresented sequences
adapter contamination
Application in Project

Used twice:

Before preprocessing
After preprocessing

This allows direct comparison of sequencing quality improvements.

Trimmomatic
Background

Trimmomatic is a read trimming tool for Illumina sequencing data.

Purpose

Remove:

adapter sequences
low-quality bases
short reads
Application in Project

Used during preprocessing to improve downstream alignment quality.

BBDuk
Background

BBDuk is part of the BBTools suite.

Purpose

Filter reads by matching them against contaminant reference sequences.

Application in Project

Removes user-specified contaminant sequences such as:

PhiX
spike-in controls
synthetic constructs

before alignment.

BWA
Background

Burrows-Wheeler Aligner (BWA) is one of the most commonly used reference alignment tools.

Purpose

Align sequencing reads to a reference genome.

Application in Project

Uses:

Shell
bwa mem
Show more lines

to align processed paired-end reads.

Samtools
Background

Samtools is the standard toolkit for SAM/BAM manipulation.

Purpose

Perform:

format conversion
sorting
duplicate marking
indexing
statistics generation
Application in Project

Used for:

Plain Text
BAM conversion
Sorting
Fixmate
Markdup
Indexing
Flagstat
Alignment statistics
Show more lines
MultiQC
Background

MultiQC combines outputs from multiple bioinformatics tools into a single report.

Purpose

Provide centralized QC reporting.

Application in Project

Aggregates:

FastQC reports
duplication metrics
alignment metrics
flagstat results
samtools statistics

into a single dashboard.

Snakemake
Background

Snakemake is a workflow management system for reproducible computational pipelines.

Purpose

Build dependency graphs and manage execution order.

Application in Project

Controls:

rule execution
dependency resolution
workflow reproducibility
Configuration File

Pipeline behavior is driven by:

config/config.yaml


Example:

YAML
sample:
accession: "SRR123456"
reference_name: "ecoli_k12"
reference_url: "https://example.org/ref.fa.gz"

trimming:
adapter_type: "TruSeq3-PE"
adapter_url: "https://example.org/adapters.fa"

contamination:
spike_ins: "resources/contaminants/phix.fa"

threads: 8

Troubleshooting
Environment Not Activated

Error:

Plain Text
Please Activate the Required Conda Environment
Show more lines

Solution:

Shell
conda activate bioinfo
Show more lines
Missing Configuration Parameters

Error:

Plain Text
MISSING:
Show more lines

Solution:

Verify required parameters exist in:

Plain Text
config/config.yaml
Show more lines
Unknown Stage

Error:

Plain Text
UNKNOWN_STAGE
Show more lines

Solution:

Run:

Shell
./scripts/run_pipeline.sh --help
Show more lines

to view available stages.

Download Failures

Downloads automatically retry three times.

If failures persist:

verify internet connectivity
verify URL validity
verify ENA availability
Checksum Failure

Error:

Plain Text
Checksum Mismatch
Show more lines

Solution:

Delete corrupted files:

Shell
rm raw/*.fastq.gz
Show more lines

and rerun pipeline.

Snakemake Validation Failure

Run:

Shell
snakemake -n
Show more lines

to inspect dependency issues without executing the workflow.

Design Principles

This project emphasizes:

reproducibility
modularity
configuration-driven execution
automated resource management
validation before execution
workflow transparency
future extensibility

The stage registry architecture separates validation, orchestration, and workflow 
execution into independent components, making the pipeline easier to maintain, test, 
and expand as additional NGS analysis modules are implemented.
